extract: The unforgiving desert of Vol'dun (/voʊl.ˈduːn/ vol-DOON) is one of the three regions of Zandalar. Previously a vibrant and lush jungle, Vol'dun is now a virtually uninhabitable, vast sea of dunes dreaded by all Zandalari, for to be exiled to its endless wastes is a sure sentence of death. And yet somehow, the wily nomads known as the vulpera have managed to eke out an existence here, despite facing a constant threat from the sethrak, a brutal snakelike race determined to reign over this arid wasteland.

Previously a vibrant and lush jungle, Vol'dun is now a virtually uninhabitable, vast sea of dunes dreaded by all [[Zandalari troll|Zandalari]], for to be exiled to its endless wastes is a sure sentence of death. And yet somehow, the wily nomads known as the [[vulpera]] have managed to eke out an existence here, despite facing a constant threat from the [[sethrak]], a brutal snakelike race determined to reign over this arid wasteland.[[:File:Blizzard Museum - Zandalar.jpg]] ==History== Thousands of years ago, this vast desert with rolling sand dunes was once a dense, vibrant jungle,{{Ref web|url=http://warcraft.blizzplanet.com/blog/comments/blizzcon-2017-world-warcraft-battle-azeroth-panel-transcript/3|title=BlizzCon 2017 World of Warcraft: Battle for Azeroth Panel Transcript - Page 3 of 12 - Blizzplanet|date=2017-11-04|accessdate=2018-09-10}}[[Vorrik#Quotes]]: {{Text|say|Vorrik|This temple is the resting place of Sethraliss, a powerful loa that protected my people from destruction long ago.}} / {{Text|say|She sacrificed herself to stop Mythrax... but with her death, the jungles of Vol'dun withered to sand.}}[[The Warguard's Trail]][[Sacred Remains (quest)]][[Tales of de Loa: Sethraliss]] described by [[Meerah]] as the jewel of the [[troll]] empire. The [[Zandalari troll]]s and the snake-like [[sethrak]] lived in harmony in this region, and together they worshiped the snake [[loa]] [[Sethraliss]].{{Ref web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8nGnT6WZbeI&t=1m10s|title=Blizzcon 2018 Interview: Alex Afrasiabi & Patrick Dawson - Story and Systems | The Lost Codex|author=The Lost Codex|work=YouTube|date=2018-11-03|accessdate=2018-11-03}} During the [[Aqir and Troll War|war]] between the trolls and the [[aqir]] roughly 16,000 years ago,{{Ref WoWCV1|70}} the [[C'Thrax]]xi warbringer [[Mythrax|Mythrax the Unraveler]] was tasked with invading Vol'dun and descended upon the region, slaughtering troll and sethrak alike. Sethraliss sacrificed herself to defeat Mythrax,[[The Keepers' Keys (Horde)]][[The Keepers' Keys (Alliance)]] but not before the C'Thrax was able to destroy the disc at the heart of [[Atul'Aman]]. Due to Sethraliss' death and the various cataclysms that occurred in the region as the years progressed, the jungles of Vol'dun were transformed into a vast desert. As a result, most of the trolls abandoned the region. This left only the sethrak, who continued to survive and thrive in Vol'dun, which they considered the holiest of holy grounds. After witnessing the destruction wrought by Mythrax firsthand, the sethrak knew that something had to be done to prevent anyone from raising the C'Thrax again. [[Sulthis]], [[Vorrik]], and [[Emperor Korthek|Korthek]] worked together to seal Mythrax within the great pyramid. Years later, Korthek grew power hungry and sought to free Mythrax to conquer [[Zuldazar]]. He gathered like-minded sethrak and declared himself emperor of the [[Faithless]]. Up until the end of the Fourth War, Zandalar sent its criminals here to die, and most of them end up perishing. The area was mostly inhabited by Zandalari vagabonds, sethrak, and [[vulpera]]. The [[Ashvane Trading Company]] also used to have a presence in the southern edge of Vol'dun, mining for [[:Azerite]]. In [[Exploring Azeroth: Islands and Isles|''Exploring Azeroth - Islands and Isles'']], it is established that Vol'dun's exiles have been called back to Zuldazar by Talanji. In addition to that, it is written that the Ancient Burrows are being reconstructed and that the Vulpera have an outpost or settlement there alongside the Vulpera Hideaway, and plans to make a joint market with the Devoted in the Scorching Sands Outpost. The conflict between the Devoted and the Faithless seems to have ended, given the introduction to Akunda that many of their respective peoples have had to move on from the war. Atul'aman is also used by young Vulpera in a new rite of passage. https://www.wowhead.com/news/updates-to-old-zones-in-exploring-azeroth-islands-and-isles-350862 ==Getting there== Vol'dun can entered through [[Nazmir]] by several roads: in [[Antul'Mita Plateau]], [[Shoaljai Tar Pits]] into [[Prisoners' Pass]], and the [[Far Reach]]. Alliance characters gain access by speaking with [[Grand Admiral Jes-Tereth]] after establishing a foothold during the [[Alliance War Campaign]]. ==Geography== [[File:Bonetrail Gulch.jpg|thumb|Bonetrail Gulch.]] Located in the north west of [[Zandalar]], Vol'dun is a vast and unforgiving land. Dunes of sand, salt flats, and bone breaking rocky terrain stretch from coast to coast, meeting up with [[Nazmir]] to the east and [[Zuldazar]] to the south. Danger here comes as much from the arid and unrelenting landscape as it does from the creatures who eke out a living here. The sand-bleached bones of giant beasts litter the land, long since picked clean and polished to a gleaming smooth by the shifting sands. Brief moments of reprieve from the heat can be found to the north in the small stretch of marsh and in the caverns and oasis tucked away from the unrelenting sun.[https://worldofwarcraft.com/en-us/news/22010731/battle-for-azeroth-vol-dun-visitor-s-guide Battle for Azeroth: Vol'dun Visitor's Guide] ===Maps and subregions=== *{{RaceIcon|Scorpion}} [[Scorpid]]s *{{RaceIcon|Kobra}} [[Serpent]]s *{{RaceIcon|GiantWasp}} [[Wasp]]s }} ==Notes and trivia== *Vol'dun's backstory is highly inconsistent, with different sources giving contradictory explanations for why the zone turned from a jungle to a desert: **At [[BlizzCon 2017]], the zone's state was explained as being due to the [[aqir]]i armies of the [[Old God]]s attacking the region thousands of years ago. However, the aqir are never even mentioned in the live version of the zone. Several models of [[silithid]] fossils exist in Vol'dun's game files but go unused in-game, suggesting that the zone's backstory was changed sometime between its announcement at BlizzCon and the release of ''Battle for Azeroth''. **At the beginning of the [[Temple of Sethraliss]] dungeon, [[Vorrik]] says that it was [[Sethraliss]]' death that caused Vol'dun's jungles to wither to sand. **In [[The Keepers' Keys (Alliance)]], Vorrik says that [[Mythrax]] destroyed the entirety of [[Atul'Aman]] and implies that it was the power unleashed from this event that caused Vol'dun's transformation. However, this is visibly contradicted by the fact that most of the pyramid is still standing, and in the [[The Keepers' Keys (Horde)|Horde version of the same quest]], Vorrik only says that the disc at the center of the pyramid was destroyed. **In an interview at [[BlizzCon 2018]], [[Alex Afrasiabi]] stated that it was Sethraliss' death combined with various cataclysms that happened in the region as the years progressed that caused Vol'dun's desertification. *The children of [[Zandalari troll|Zandalari]] who were banished to Vol'dun used to be exiled alongside their parents, but this is no longer the case.[[Mugjabu#Quotes]] **A chain of exemption is required for being allowed to leave Vol'dun, to prevent exiled trolls from escaping. [[Chain of Exemption]] *Neutral "sleeping" [[lasher]]s can be found in large quantities in Vol'dun.
